definitions.gloss: copying verbatim; wholesale copying; transcribing in full
definitions.explanation: Copying something exactly as it is, word for word, without any changes or original input. Often carries a negative connotation, implying laziness, plagiarism, or lack of effort.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}の{宿題|しゅくだい}を{丸写|まるうつ}しした。
examples.english: I copied my friend's homework word for word.

examples.japanese: ネットの{記事|きじ}を{丸写|まるうつ}しにしたレポートは{不合格|ふごうかく}になる。
examples.english: A report that's a wholesale copy of an online article will get a failing grade.

examples.japanese: {参考書|さんこうしょ}の{丸写|まるうつ}しではなく、{自分|じぶん}の{言葉|ことば}でまとめることが{大事|だいじ}だ。
examples.english: It's important to summarize things in your own words rather than just copying the reference book verbatim.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost always used negatively, implying someone took a shortcut instead of doing their own work. Very common in school and academic contexts. Can be used as a noun ({丸写|まるうつ}し) or with する ({丸写|まるうつ}しにする / {丸写|まるうつ}しする).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {丸写|まるうつ}しにする (to copy verbatim)
- {丸写|まるうつ}しのレポート (a word-for-word copied report)
- {答|こた}えを{丸写|まるうつ}しする (to copy answers wholesale)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- コピペ: copy-paste — modern slang for copying digital text
- {盗用|とうよう}: plagiarism — more formal and severe
